desk.meaning: Recognizable trading workstation, software and cursor; chart updates are data, cursor is manual attention.
desk.geometry: Beveled8.8×5.5 monitor at y4.2; front screen z.22. Layered metal shell, vented back, jointed stand,9.8×5.6 wood desk, individually modelled keycaps, mouse seam, lamp and cable loops. Chart uses actual 3D candlestick bodies/wicks registered to its screen coordinates.
desk.layers: Near keyboard/mouse; screen with actual chart and rule inspector; distant wall, lamp pool and shelf. Local screen light illuminates bezel/desk.
desk.motion: One chart identity with explicit sample-time rewind for BEFORE SIGNAL. Cursor screen-coordinate travel and button depression consume notice/manual-check/manual-submit. Configuration, closing tests and status use their named events.
desk.risks: No free-floating screen card, no long unattended full-device hold, no threshold/order confusion; text must fit at screen closeups.
desk.technique: Parent the OHLC geometry and canvas UI to the same monitor. Convert price to height with (price−99.90)/0.18 × chartHeight. The screen is at local z=.17; candles at z=.225, pointer z=.50. Camera can begin in front of individual extruded candles and pull out without swapping footage. 8.9×5.55×.30 monitor, 8.3×5 screen, 12×.32×6.4 desk. Keyboard: 5×15 keys with one spacebar. Wall and lamp establish physical scale. Use original candle body height when scaling the last candle; dividing by a generic minimum exaggerates price moves. The screen painter consumes deskDisplayState; its complete serialized state is the texture cache key, including late definition highlighting and current price. test-end reveals one, two, then three historical outcomes in sequence; the monitor-end word anchor restores the chart before the camera leaves the test area. Reporting uses the shared reported flag, not an earlier opacity threshold.
desk.lighting: Cool display fill reflects on the metal bezel and keycaps; warm point light under the desk lamp supplies a localized amber pool. Object motion changes specular response; lights are fixed.
desk.hold: Monitor shell, keyboard, mouse, lamp, desk and wall retain their transforms. The last candle follows the market-change event; only the closing shot adds a small continuing quote oscillation. No live trading connection exists.
desk.adjustable: Event frames, camera knots, OHLC data and render settings are specification inputs. Dimensions and geometry formulas above are component-library constants; changing their construction requires authoring and a new moving proof.
desk.constraints: Keep identity and numeric state consistent across builders; use global frame evaluation, no accumulated delta-time. Typography must fit at both720px and360px. Light/material changes are not substitutes for a meaningful event.

configuration.meaning: Stored chart condition, fixed quantity3 and limit100.05 enlarged as data relationships.
configuration.geometry: Chart plane with extruded candles; vertical price axis. Threshold and limit are separate fixed horizontal world lines. Three quantity tiles are linked to SIZE3 by fine leaders. All positions use explicit price-to-height mapping.
configuration.layers: Foreground active parameter, underlying chart, dim related parameters and subtle depth grid.
configuration.motion: Condition-detail raises chart into view; size-detail fans exactly3units; limit-detail extends fixed100.05 boundary. Continuous chart remains subordinate.
configuration.risks: Never imply configuring an order is submitting it; no knobs or press metaphor.
configuration.technique: Enlarge the same 27-row OHLC array to a 5.5×3 chart; use the same numerical price projection for candle heights, ticks, threshold and limit. Three .55 cubes fan in X as size-detail progresses; their group grows from .05 to1. The100.05plane spans6.6×3.6 and grows only in X. The camera changes target from chart to quantity to price axis; all three share one root.
configuration.lighting: Metal candle edges catch the studio rim. Cyan quantity bodies and the amber price plane separate quantity from price; the plane is translucent, not a solid obstruction.
configuration.hold: Price axis, threshold100.00 and the limit100.05 are fixed. Quantity contains exactly three units. These are configuration values; nothing in this family submits an order.

data.meaning: Market price/time records enter a software condition; false evaluation creates no instruction.
data.geometry: Batched atlas field of timestamped market records, each with real price text; bevelled selected sample5.23×5.25frontplane and A23 ray-mapped1.85×inspection lens. Separate threshold graph, history column, empty outgoing slot and instruction assembly region.
data.layers: Near selected record/lens; orderly midground quotes; long vanishing rows. Warm selected sample contrasts with cool field.
data.motion: Inspect extracts one actual field record; failures move to history and keep output empty. Pass changes sample100.01 above100.00. Condition, side,size,limit assemble O-01 only on build.
data.risks: Lens must use same sample texture; selected sample changes on cue; no generic TRUE token instead of numeric evidence.
data.technique: One 2048² atlas has8×8 quote cells. Instanced plane1.22² and body1.25×.12×1.25 share18×32 positions spaced1.4. The dataField input supplies rows, columns, spacing, bendStart8, bendRadius24 and speed.48. Beyond8worldunits, rows follow a24-unit circular bend: z=−8−24sin(angle), y=.1+24(1−cos(angle)); angle=(depth−8)/24. Box normals and text planes rotate together, preserving .066normal offset and legibility. Each row wraps over the full32-row length independently; the entire field never resets by one row at once. This carries the same timestamps from foreground floor into a layered data horizon rather than an empty backdrop. Each instance carries tileUv; onBeforeCompile maps both diffuse and emissive UVs to the same cell. Selected card uses a1000² canvas on5.23×5.25plane. inspectionLens computes optical coordinates from this exact face and camera, magnifying1.85×; do not render unrelated text in the lens. The lens enters and leaves along an explicit18-frame trajectory inside its staging window, without a visibility pop. Numeric values99.98/99.99 fail;100.01 crosses100.00. Condition qualification remains above the4.1×2.6ticket. BUY3 and LIMIT100.05 move into separate rows atY3.03 and2.40, never the same center. Ticket fields remain hidden until build completes, then the landed values replace the floating labels. This prevents duplicate type and overlapping values.
data.lighting: Atlas textures are emissive at .38 with standard metal response. A warm point light rises with passes and fades as instruction assembly completes. Lens rings reflect the studio while the lens samples the selected face.
data.hold: 576 quote faces continue advancing in long rows. Selected sample, history and outgoing area remain distinct. The outgoing region stays empty until build; no false sample generates an order.

Hide the hero rack AND port plate when route>.36 and ingress line when route>.30 to avoid a near-camera obstruction. Camera shares the port axis and approaches the illuminated inner path.

acceptance.meaning: Venue acceptance and actual execution are distinct states.
acceptance.geometry: Paired broker/venue racks around a recessed application status display; dimensional order ticket and three empty quantity outlines.
acceptance.layers: O-01 hero, status display and hardware, distant populated rack rows.
acceptance.motion: Route completion causes ACCEPTED. not-filled holds FILLED0 and three empty outlines. Camera follows ticket into next book.
acceptance.risks: No early fill and no teleport without match cut.
acceptance.technique: Stage two compactRack props around a4.3×2.8ticket and three.72×.6×.6empty wire cells. The ticket enters by a slight rotation/depth settle driven by not-filled. Keep the order identity/quantity/limit from O-01; do not infer fill from packet arrival.
acceptance.lighting: Rack metal remains cool; filled-zero text has a restrained warm accent. No fill flash is used for an acknowledgment.
acceptance.hold: The acknowledged instruction remains ACCEPTED, FILLED0. Three wireframe quantity cells remain empty. Their small vertical motion is supporting movement, not a new event.

book.meaning: Finite available quantity meets a limit order at eligible prices; remainder persists.
book.geometry: Four dimensional price-depth rows100.03/.04/.05/.06 with explicit price-to-height mapping, horizontal quantity bars made of unit cells, and three-slot order. Thin100.05plane is fixed. Execution records sit below matching region.
book.layers: Near incoming order; mid price/quantity ladder; background continuation of many muted price levels and grid.
book.motion: 100.04unit withdraws; two100.03units follow curves into distinct order cells exactly on fills; third outline remains. Above-limit reveals100.06 excluded by100.05.
book.risks: Matched endpoints identical; no volume creation, no third fill; price axis must read clearly at phone scale.
book.technique: Map price to world Y=1.25+(price−100.03)×110. Rows100.03/.04/.05/.06 contain2/1/0/4units. Units are.58×.46×.72; incoming order has3wire slots .72×.55×.82. The100.04unit translates5units inX and disappears only after withdrawal completes. Each100.03unit follows start.lerp(end,p) plus sin(πp)×.6 inY; filled replacement appears exactly atp=1 so quantity is conserved. A100.05plane separates the remaining slot from ineligible100.06liquidity. Distinct execution labels appear only after their own matches and leave when attention moves to the remaining quantity. The book shots use captionY1140 to keep records clear.
book.lighting: Cyan available units become warm filled order cells at contact. A short gold point-light pulse accompanies the second match. The translucent price boundary gains contrast on above-limit.
book.hold: Eligible100.03 units transfer once; withdrawn100.04 quantity does not return. Third requested slot remains an empty outline. Four100.06 units remain above the fixed100.05 limit.

report.meaning: Report is data returned after execution, with the same order identity and quantities.
report.geometry: Two filled execution rows physically join a structured electronic report; report travels into a dimensional application record. Field name/value pairs are legible, exact, connected to their sources.
report.layers: Near moving report fields, software record, fading book rows behind.
report.motion: report-form creates R-01 after fills; report-return moves the same group and updates requested3/filled2/remaining1 simultaneously.
report.risks: No report before execution, no paper output, no unexplained number changes.
report.technique: Stack two3.7×.75execution rows vertically; move toward a5.5×4.4report. Hide source rows at formationp=.62 and reveal the report at that same boundary. Formation must finish before return begins. Return shrinks the same report toward a7×4.8monitor, exposing the application. Requested/filled/remaining update together at returnp>.8; report stays separate until its return is nearly complete. Keep R-01→O-01 linkage.
report.lighting: The electronic report uses cool field names and amber filled quantity. Rear record lines supply depth; no printer or paper geometry exists.
report.hold: Two execution records are immutable inputs to R-01. After receipt, requested3,filled2,remaining1 stay unchanged while the record remains readable.

comparison.meaning: Attention delay differs; neither view predicts prices nor guarantees fill or profit.
comparison.geometry: Two vertically stacked dimensional charts share exact dataset/threshold and marked sample. Cursor path in manual view, stored-rule trace in configured view. Both converge into a single full chart.
comparison.layers: First manual chart, second configured chart, common price history and depth axis.
comparison.motion: Automatic action event originates one instruction; manual waits then acts. On no-prediction the two chart representations merge and future candles form up/down independently; result remains partial.
comparison.risks: No stopwatch, race outcome or invented speed advantage measurement; no P/L curve.
comparison.technique: Stack6.6×2.9panels atY5.2/1.9, with5.4×1.55charts from the shared array. The final candle crosses100.00 during compare. A ring identifies the same sample in each view. automatic-action and manual-action trace from that sample through RULE-01 or the cursor/button into two separately labeled3-unit/100.05instruction tickets; the camera visits each origin. These are alternative illustrations, not two live orders. no-prediction moves bothYpositions toward3.5; keep a.2depth separation to prevent z-fighting and hide the rear copy after.98. Hide MANUAL/PREDEFINED titles on merge and reveal MARKET KEEPS MOVING. Six new candles reveal sequentially after the merge while the prior sample stays fixed; the chart translates left to make room. No outcome or profit is inferred.
comparison.lighting: Shared charts use identical lighting/materials so neither is presented as a winning result. Warm action markers identify instructions, not profits.
comparison.hold: Both views use the same OHLC history and threshold. Manual attention differs from configured evaluation. At merge, both become the same market; partial fill remains2+1, with no profit outcome.
